drills.q: A table visual shows the same Total Sales number on every row. Why?
drills.a: Filter context isn't differentiating rows: no dimension from the fact is on the view (or the measure aggregates over a context the rows don't slice). The fix is model/grain — put a real dimension on the axis — not a new formula.

drills.q: Write the YoY % measure and name its two prerequisites.
drills.a: YoY % := DIVIDE([Total Sales] - CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODYEARAGO('Date'[Date])), CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODYEARAGO('Date'[Date]))). Prerequisites: a proper date dimension, MARKED as date table, related to the fact — time intelligence navigates nothing without it.

drills.q: Why is 'Sales Amount' as a calculated column a modeling error?
drills.a: A column is row-context, computed at refresh and STORED — it bloats the model and freezes the value outside filter context. Total Sales := SUM(Sales[Amount]) as a measure computes per query under whatever slicing is active. Columns only for row-level attributes that must slice.

drills.q: When is DirectQuery the right choice despite its costs?
drills.a: Three cases: real-time freshness requirements, facts too large for capacity, and security/compliance policies requiring data never leave the source. Costs to name up front: slower interactions, DAX dialect limitations, source-load responsibility. Default remains Import; Direct Lake is the Fabric-era middle.

drills.q: A user sees rows they shouldn't. Walk the RLS debugging order.
drills.a: 1) Workspace membership — admins/members BYPASS RLS entirely (the deployment trap). 2) Role membership — which roles does the user hold; effective access = intersection. 3) Role DAX — the predicate logic and dynamic-username matching. Tested with View-as-role / test-as-user.

drills.q: In Tableau, your {FIXED [region]: SUM(sales)} disagrees with the sheet's percent-of-total under a state filter. Which is wrong?
drills.a: Neither — the disagreement is the semantics: FIXED computes at declared region grain regardless of view filters; percent-of-total (a table calc) respects them. Explaining that cleanly is the entire point of the question.

drills.q: A Tableau date pill turned green and the bar chart became a line. What happened?
drills.a: Blue = discrete (headers, categorical bars); green = continuous (axis, line). The date pill switched from discrete to continuous/exact — pill color encodes the computation the viz runs. The four-quadrant model (dimension/measure x discrete/continuous) is Tableau's grammar.

drills.q: Two dashboards, two different YoY numbers for the same month. Give the debugging order and the class fix.
drills.a: 1) Different datasets (no shared certified model — the most common org failure). 2) Different calendars (fiscal vs calendar). 3) Unmarked date table breaking SAMEPERIODYEARAGO. 4) Filter-context differences (one hard-filters region). 5) Drifted duplicate measures. Class fix: certified shared semantic model + measure library.

drills.q: Dashboard is slow. Give the triage order — and what's wrong with 'just remove charts' as the whole answer.
drills.a: 1) Visuals per page (each is a query). 2) Model tier: calculated-column bloat, many-to-many fan-out. 3) Storage mode: DirectQuery per-visual source roundtrips vs Import. 4) DAX/LOD patterns: FILTER over whole tables, iterator chains. 'Fewer charts' is step one of four — the follow-up 'still slow after cutting visuals?' exists to catch candidates whose whole model is chart-count.

drills.q: Can you build a Power BI dashboard in Desktop? Explain the object model.
drills.a: No — dashboards (pin tiles from reports) exist only in the Service. Desktop builds reports; the Service publishes/shares/refreshes/governs: workspaces, apps, gateways for on-prem refresh, deployment pipelines dev->test->prod.

drills.q: Slicer filters one visual but not another. Why, structurally?
drills.a: Filter propagation travels through model relationships — the untouched visual's table has no relationship path to the slicer's field (unrelated tables need a bridge/shared dimension). Slicers aren't page-wide magic; the star schema's edges ARE the propagation.

drills.q: Answer 'Power BI or Tableau?' as a senior candidate would.
drills.a: Estate decides: Microsoft/Fabric gravity, governed enterprise reporting, bundling -> Power BI near-default; viz-craft culture, analyst exploration, Salesforce adjacency -> Tableau. Neither easier — DAX filter-context is the deeper modeling concept, Tableau viz-craft the deeper presentation one. Tool religion reads as never having operated in an estate.
